task: Score-interpretability calibration (field-report recommendation #2): measure the noise floor (nonsense-query controls) and real-signal score band of the shipped six-leg pipeline, on two index sizes, so README can publish an evidence-backed score-reading recipe instead of an absolute threshold that can never fire.
method: Five nonsense control queries (no corpus term overlap) and all 66 labelled queries run through eval/harness.rank_episodes_for_query (the production leg sequence) against two indexes built from different corpus states. noise_floor_max = highest top-result score any nonsense query achieved; the real band is the distribution of top-result scores across labelled queries.

findings.absolute_thresholds_cannot_work: max real-query top score is 0.0964; any absolute bar like 0.30 discards every result the pipeline can produce. Scores are weighted RRF sums (six legs of w/(60+rank)) -- their magnitude is set by the fusion constants, not by a 0-1 relevance scale.
findings.separation_is_thin: median real top score (0.067) is only ~2.0x the measured noise-floor max (0.034). Genuinely valuable hits can score within 1.5-2x of noise -- the field report's two decision-changing results scored 0.054 and 0.072 on a larger corpus with a lower floor.
findings.corpus_size_scaling: between 5,148 and 7,348 chunks the score distributions are essentially identical (rank-structure dominates), but the field deployment measured a 2x lower noise floor on a 14,725-episode corpus: the floor falls as corpus size rises, so raw scores are NOT comparable across indexes of very different sizes and merging multi-index results by raw score systematically favors the smaller index.
findings.recipe: to set a quality bar on YOUR index: run 2-3 nonsense queries, take the max top-score as the noise floor, and treat ~1.5x that value as the lowest plausibly-relevant score -- expecting real hits to start barely above it.
